meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_94_packages.json, the single reference===94 bechina edge from torahData.js, and the full source text torah_94.txt. Scanned every line of the source text for explicit bechina language: בְּחִינַת, הוּא/הִיא (equating two concepts), נִקְרָא, לְשׁוֹן, הַיְנוּ in an equative context, and הֵם in a definitional equating context. Each candidate was checked against torahData.js for whether a bechina edge with reference===94 already exists.

analysis_notes.summary: All 2 bechina-connected nodes (אמונה, אלקי אביך) are assigned to Package 1. No unassigned dataset nodes exist. However, the source text of Torah #94 is rich with bechina-language statements that are entirely absent from torahData.js. These represent significant gaps in the dataset's coverage of this Torah.

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.source_quote: נִמְצָא כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָא לְבוּשׁ
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.analysis: The Rebbe states that every individual Israelite IS CALLED a garment (לבוש). 'נִקְרָא' is explicit bechina language. This establishes a bechina: ישראל ↔ לבוש. The teaching opens with this equation as the foundation for explaining why the worlds were created for Israel — Israel IS God's garment/glory. This pair would belong to a proposed new package centered on כבוד / לבוש / ישראל (see new_packages file). Polarity: good.
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.suggested_package: NEW — כבוד וישראל (see torah_94_new_packages.json, Package A)

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.source_quote: וּלְבוּשׁ נִקְרָא כָּבוֹד, כִּי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן קָרֵי לְמָאנֵהּ מְכַבְּדוּתָא
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.analysis: The garment IS CALLED honor/glory (כבוד). 'נִקְרָא' is explicit bechina language. Rabbi Yochanan called his clothing 'that which honors me' — so garments and glory share the same nature: both are the external expression of inner worth/presence. This pair לבוש ↔ כבוד is a bechina statement. It would connect with ישראל ↔ לבוש into the כבוד cluster. Polarity: good.
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.suggested_package: NEW — כבוד וישראל (see torah_94_new_packages.json, Package A)

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.source_quote: וּכְבוֹדִי הַיְנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, דִּכְתִיב: וְשָׁכַנְתִּי בְּתוֹכָם
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.analysis: The Rebbe states explicitly: 'כְּבוֹדִי הַיְנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל' — My glory IS Israel. 'הַיְנוּ' is quintessential bechina language. Combined with ישראל↔לבוש and לבוש↔כבוד, this creates a 3-node chain: ישראל ↔ לבוש ↔ כבוד, all sharing the same essential nature. Polarity: good.
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.suggested_package: NEW — כבוד וישראל (see torah_94_new_packages.json, Package A)

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.analysis: The divine sparks ARE letters. 'הֵם' in this definitional equating context is bechina language. The sparks and the letters are two names for the same reality: the compressed divine vitality hidden in every created thing. This bechina ניצוצות ↔ אותיות is the core mechanism of the Torah's teaching about elevating sparks. Polarity: good (they are holy divine light).
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.suggested_package: NEW — ניצוצות ואותיות (see torah_94_new_packages.json, Package B)

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.source_quote: כִּי הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת הֵם הַחִיּוּת שֶׁל הַדָּבָר
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.analysis: The sparks ARE the vitality (חיות) of the thing. This is another explicit equating statement: ניצוצות ↔ חיות. The sparks do not merely produce vitality — they ARE the vitality. This belongs with the ניצוצות cluster. Polarity: good.

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.source_quote: וְהָאוֹתִיּוֹת הֵם צִמְצוּמִים, עַד כָּאן אוֹת א', עַד כָּאן אוֹת ת'
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.analysis: The letters ARE contractions (צמצומים). This is a profound bechina: the letters of divine speech are themselves the contractions (tzimtzumim) that limit and bound the infinite divine light so it can be received. The letters and the tzimtzum share the same essential nature: they are the bounding vessels of infinite light. This would add צמצום as a bechina node of אותיות. Polarity: neutral (tzimtzum is a structural cosmic mechanism, neither good nor evil in itself, but here used in the service of the good: enabling the world to receive divine blessing).

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.analysis: The word 'Know' (דע from 'דַּע אֶת אֱלֹקֵי אָבִיךָ') IS wisdom and intellect. 'הִיא' is equating language. This establishes: דע ↔ חכמה. Polarity: good.

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.source_quote: וְחָכְמָה הִיא יוּ"ד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁפֵּרֵשׁ רַשִׁ"י: יָשִׁיר — יוּ"ד עַל שֵׁם הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה נֶאֶמְרָה
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.analysis: Wisdom IS the letter yod (י). 'הִיא' is explicit equating (bechina) language. The yod, being the smallest letter, represents the first point of thought/intellect — it equals חכמה in the sefirotic map. Rashi's commentary on 'יָשִׁיר' ('the yod refers to thought') grounds this in a textual proof. This establishes חכמה ↔ יוד. Polarity: good.

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.source_quote: וְעוֹד, הָעַיִן הוּא חָכְמָה, כִּי חַכְמֵי הָעֵדָה נִקְרָאִים עֵינֵי הָעֵדָה
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.analysis: The eye IS wisdom. 'הוּא' is explicit equating (bechina) language. Furthermore, 'חַכְמֵי הָעֵדָה נִקְרָאִים עֵינֵי הָעֵדָה' — the wise are CALLED the eyes of the congregation (Numbers 15). Both 'הוּא' and 'נִקְרָאִים' are bechina language. This is the geometric proof too: ז×י = ע (7×10=70), so the zayin+yod combination equals ayin. This establishes עין ↔ חכמה. Polarity: good.

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.source_quote: וְעָשִׂיתָ צִּיץ זָהָב טָהוֹר, צִיץ — מִלְּשׁוֹן הִסְתַּכְּלוּת
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.analysis: The tzitz (priestly headplate) IS the language of gazing/looking (הסתכלות). 'מִלְּשׁוֹן' is standard bechina language in Rebbe Nachman's terminology. The tzitz on the High Priest's forehead represents the pure gaze of wisdom — when one looks at the world with the pure eye of faith+wisdom, one elevates the sparks. This establishes ציץ ↔ הסתכלות. Polarity: good.

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.source_quote: וּמִן הָאֱמוּנָה הַזֶּה נַעֲשֶׂה זַיִ"ן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְכָל מַעֲשֵׂהוּ בֶּאֱמוּנָה, וְהָעֲשִׂיָּה הִיא שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַחֹל, וְהָאֱמוּנָה הִיא הַשְּׁבִיעִית
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.analysis: The proof text says faith produces (נַעֲשֶׂה) the zayin — this is primarily eitza language (cause-and-effect: faith → zayin). However, the additional equating statement 'הָאֱמוּנָה הִיא הַשְּׁבִיעִית' (faith IS the seventh) does use 'הִיא' equating language. The zayin (=7) and faith share a structural identity: both are the seventh in a sequence of seven (ז = the seventh letter; שביעית = the seventh day/quality). The Rebbe links them via the verse 'וְכָל מַעֲשֵׂהוּ בֶּאֱמוּנָה' where 'מַעֲשֵׂהוּ' refers to the six days of action and 'בֶּאֱמוּנָה' is the seventh. This is a borderline case — the primary relationship is eitza (faith produces zayin), not pure bechina. However, 'הָאֱמוּנָה הִיא הַשְּׁבִיעִית' does establish a bechina of faith=seventh. If added as a bechina node, זיין would extend Package 1 (אמונה).
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.caveat: The relationship between אמונה and זיין in Torah #94 is primarily eitza (faith produces zayin via gematria). The statement 'הָאֱמוּנָה הִיא הַשְּׁבִיעִית' could support a bechina interpretation. Mark as lower-confidence gap — include in dataset review but do not add to packages without editorial confirmation.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: The Rebbe says 'הָאוֹתִיּוֹת נַעֲשִׂים דִּבּוּרִים' — letters BECOME speech. This is eitza language (letters produce speech), not bechina (letters ARE speech). Excluded: this is cause-and-effect, not shared nature.

The Rebbe cites 'בְּרָאתִיו יְצַרְתִּיו אַף עֲשִׂיתִיו' to prove the worlds were created for Israel's glory. He interprets these as three modes of creation (beriah/yetzira/asiyah) but does not use bechina language to equate them with other concepts. They appear as proof-text, not bechina nodes.

The verse interpretation 'רָאוּ כָּל אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ — הַיְנוּ הָאַרְצִיּוּת שֶׁל הַדָּבָר נַעֲשֶׂה אֶפֶס' uses הַיְנוּ but in the sense of 'that is to say, the earthliness becomes nothing' — this is an interpretive paraphrase of a verse, establishing what happens (eitza) when sparks are elevated, not a bechina of ארציות with another concept.

Line 3 states 'יֵשׁ לוֹ צַעַר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: בְּכָל צָרָתָם לוֹ צָר' — this cites a verse about God sharing Israel's suffering. It is a theological statement, not a bechina equation between two concepts. Excluded.
